personas.name: routine-characterise-lesion-skin-lesion-complete
personas.description: Well-formed routine referral: a changing pigmented skin lesion, excised skin-lesion specimen requested (first-line for characterise-lesion), properly fixed in formalin and confirmed labelled with a specimen count recorded, every completeness field present — expect usually-appropriate + ok specimen quality + routine + accept.

indication.clinicalQuestion: Irregular pigmented lesion on the left forearm, changing in size over 3 months — characterise for malignancy.
indication.clinicalDetails: No personal or family history of melanoma. Lesion excised in clinic under local anaesthetic.

triage.notes: Excision margins marked with sutures for orientation.

firedRules.description: Requested skin-lesion specimen is the recommended sample for "characterise-lesion".
Fixative, labelling, and specimen count are satisfactory.
No escalation; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).

personas.name: two-week-wait-suspected-malignancy-biopsy-fixative-other-caution
personas.description: Colonoscopic biopsies from a suspicious sigmoid colon mass: biopsy is the recommended (ideal) specimen for the suspected-malignancy indication, and the indication itself auto-escalates triage onto the two-week-wait suspected-cancer pathway regardless of the routine urgency requested; the endoscopy unit's non-standard fixative forces a specimen-quality caution — expect usually-appropriate + caution specimen quality + two-week-wait + accept.

indication.clinicalQuestion: Colonoscopic biopsies from a sigmoid colon mass — confirm or exclude adenocarcinoma.
indication.clinicalDetails: FIT-positive screening; mass seen on colonoscopy with contact bleeding.

triage.notes: Colorectal MDT discussion planned once histology is available. Non-standard fixative used by the endoscopy unit — confirm suitability.

firedRules.description: Requested biopsy specimen is the recommended sample for "suspected-malignancy".
Fixative recorded as "other"; confirm suitability for histology.

flags.suggestedAction: Expedite accessioning and reporting on the suspected-cancer (NICE NG12) pathway.

flags.description: Fixative recorded as "other"; suitability for histology not confirmed.
flags.suggestedAction: Confirm the fixative used is appropriate for histological processing.

personas.name: query-referrer-inflammatory-disease-other-specimen-mismatch-fresh-unfixed-incomplete
personas.description: A skin biopsy sent fresh (unfixed) without formalin, container labelling unconfirmed, and specimen count not recorded: fresh tissue submitted outside a frozen-section pathway is at reject-risk for autolysis, which forces query-referrer ahead of the appropriateness check; an 'other' specimen type was also requested even though biopsy / endoscopic-biopsy are recommended for the inflammatory-disease indication, an independent mismatch; several administrative fields are not yet captured — expect usually-not-appropriate + reject-risk specimen quality + routine + query-referrer, completeness below 100.

indication.clinicalDetails: Chronic itchy rash for 6 months, suspected inflammatory dermatosis; biopsy sent fresh in error without formalin.

triage.notes: Specimen sent to the lab without fixative; container not clearly labelled.

firedRules.description: Requested other specimen is not usually appropriate for "inflammatory-disease"; query the referrer.
Fresh (unfixed) specimen submitted outside a frozen-section pathway — autolysis / drying risk.
Specimen container labelling not confirmed — mislabel risk.
Number of specimen containers / pots not recorded.
No escalation; triage follows the requested urgency (routine).

flags.description: Specimen fixation is inadequate (fresh / unfixed outside a frozen-section pathway, or no fixative recorded).
flags.suggestedAction: Contact the requester urgently; the specimen may be unfit for diagnosis without prompt fixation.
Verify the specimen container is labelled with patient identifiers matching the request before accessioning.
Query the referrer for the specific question the report should answer.
